name: The Chain Bridge
unique_feature: a bridge hung on four chains each forged by a different clan, across the gorge to Kharrow Hold
story: Each chain is a treaty. When a clan is shamed its chain is loosened one link, and the bridge leans.
encounter: a toll-keeper NPC; crag-wolves on the far approach at night

name: The Rib Cathedral
unique_feature: a giant's ribcage you walk through like a nave, each rib taller than a hall
story: The clans hold the Moot's oaths here because a giant's bones do not forget. Crag-wolves den in the skull at the far end.
encounter: crag-wolf pack in the skull; the ribs give cover from their knockdown charges; Ymma ko-Dreugh keeps the oaths in the nave

name: The Three Sisters
unique_feature: three terraced falls with a Hearthstone on the middle ledge behind the water
story: Three sisters of clan Rudd carried the Hearthstone up so their brother, exiled, could still be remembered somewhere warm.
encounter: none; scree-hags on the cliffs above shriek at climbers

name: The Clanless Camp
unique_feature: an overhang camp where exiled warriors have hung their loosened chain links as wind chimes
story: Every raider here was once someone's chain. They take from Brindlecrag's ore carts and claim it as their blood-price.
encounter: elite raiders in heavy plate; a brute and two skirmishers; approach along the ledge above the overhang

name: The Finger Shrine
unique_feature: a sinkhole whose central pillar is a giant's finger bone carved with memory-songs
story: The memory-keeper of clan Kharrow adds a line each year. The finger belongs to the Fallen Hand; nobody has explained how it got here.

name: The Watch of the Gate
unique_feature: the clan toll-house at Windgate, half buried in old snow, its bell frozen mid-swing
story: The soft northern edge. The gate-warden takes a toll for a pass nobody can cross until spring, and spring has not come in years.
encounter: none; the pass beyond is closed by avalanche

name: The Seven Stones
unique_feature: seven stones for seven clans, each grown over with a different colour of lichen
story: When a clan dies its stone loses its lichen within a year; there are seven stones and six clans, and the seventh is still green.
encounter: none; a survey point over the high moor

name: The Hidden Tarn
unique_feature: a high tarn behind a wall of scree, black and perfectly still, under the Cradle's mouth
story: The scree-hags fish it with their hands. Nothing lives in the water, and they still catch things.
encounter: scree-hags on the scree; ambushers and stone-throwers, silence their shrieks first

name: Kharrow Gate
unique_feature: a clan gate-tower at the mouth of Kharrow Gorge where the North Road enters the heights and blood-price begins
story: Travellers are told the law here: what is taken is paid for in kind, a death in blood-price, and a host is never robbed. The gate-ward asks each traveller to say it back.
hook: A traveller refused to say the law back and walked on; the clans want to know what she is.

name: Ghast's Broken Bridge
unique_feature: a chain bridge across Ghast Dale with one chain cut, hanging askew in the gorge since the year of the broken bridge
story: The chain Ghast cut was Kharrow's. Nobody has crossed in two hundred years, except goats, who do not know about the Moot.
encounter: crag-wolves den under the anchor stones
hook: Cross it, and read the mark on the far anchor that belongs to no clan.

name: Brindle Swallow
unique_feature: three cairns round a swallow-hole where Brindle Beck drops out of the world and is heard a mile underground
story: The beck falls into the hole and comes out a day later and colder at Brindlecrag's spring. The miners say it passes the singing shaft on the way.
hook: Drop a bell into Brindle Swallow and listen for it at Brindlecrag's spring.

name: The Smeltings
unique_feature: Brindle's smelting kilns below the village, the ore-carts drawn up by their mouths
story: Iron from the top of the vein, lead from the middle and silver from the bottom, which is smelted at night with the doors shut and the pipes playing.
hook: The silver has come out of the kiln with a ring in it, and struck it hums a note the smiths refuse to name.

name: Old Eld
unique_feature: an abandoned silver working on the edge, its shaft sealed with a door of bone
story: The first silver working on Brindle Edge, sealed when the singing started at Oskeld. The bone door is a giant's shoulder-blade, and it is warm.
encounter: a stone-thrall walks the working after dark
hook: Open the bone door at Old Eld.

name: The Jawbone
unique_feature: a giant's jaw standing on end like a gate at the head of Oskeld Dale, the rest of the skull sunk in the moor
story: Oskel herds go through the Jawbone every spring on the way up and every autumn on the way down. A beast that balks is sold, not eaten.
encounter: crag-wolves wait in the heather beyond it
hook: Every beast in a herd balked at the Jawbone this spring.

name: The Giant's Spine
unique_feature: a giant's spine lying along the head of Ribdale with a clan cairn raised on every vertebra
story: The clans say the Rib Cathedral's ribs belong to this spine, which would make the giant a mile long. The Sayers say two giants. The clans say the Sayers have not counted the vertebrae.
encounter: stone-thralls stand up among the vertebrae
hook: Count the vertebrae.

name: Kharrow Force
unique_feature: the Skerrow Water leaping in one fall into the head of Kharrow Gorge, a rope of iron links strung across its lip for the brave to cross
story: Kharrow youths cross the lip on their naming day. The ones who fall are fished out at the Hold, a mile down, and are named anyway, but differently.
hook: Cross the lip of Kharrow Force and the clans will name you for it.

name: Rudd Pike Beacon
unique_feature: a clan beacon on Rudd Pike whose fire-bowl is lit when the Windgate avalanche comes down
story: When the Long Snow slides on the Windgate, Rudd Pike burns and every hold shuts its doors. It burned for the winter of the long snow, and Rudd have not let anybody forget it.
hook: Rudd Pike Beacon burned last night, and the Windgate snow did not move.

name: The Snow Shelter
unique_feature: a stone shelter on the Windgate road with a bell on a pole for travellers caught by the weather
story: The gate-warden keeps it stocked with peat and oatcake. The bell is rung by anyone caught out, and whoever hears it goes, which is the one law older than the Moot.
hook: The shelter bell rang on a clear night, and whoever rang it was gone when the gate-warden came.

name: Kharrow's Cairns
unique_feature: three memory-cairns above the gorge where every Kharrow who died on the mountain is named once a year
story: Ushka ko-Kharrow kept the memory forty-one years and lost no name; these are the cairns she sang them at.
hook: Dunna ko-Kharrow wants the cairns' names checked against the Rope-Song, and one of them is not in it.

name: The Blood-Price Stones
unique_feature: three stones by the North Road with grooves worn in their tops where blood-price is paid in laid coin
story: A clan owed a death is paid here, in public, on the road, so every traveller sees that it was. The coin lies in the grooves a day before it is taken up.
hook: There is coin in the grooves for a death nobody has reported.

name: The Giants' Stair
unique_feature: a stair of steps each as high as a man, cut up the wall toward the north by something with longer legs
story: The giants' last road, the clans say, going north past the Windgate into the Ice Reach. It stops at a sheer face where the snow has never melted.
encounter: a stone-thrall sits on the top step
hook: Climb to where the Giants' Stair stops and read what is cut in the last riser.

name: The Bonefield
unique_feature: a scree slope where giant bones lie as thick as fallen timber, bleached and furred with lichen
story: Skarl herders gather bone here for lintels and tokens. They take only what has come loose on its own, and leave a stone for each piece.
encounter: stone-thralls rise out of the scree
hook: The Bonefield's bones have started to lie in order.

name: Ghorrow
unique_feature: an eighth hold cut into the cliff with no clan's mark over its door, and eight doors inside, seven of them bricked
story: The clans say Ghorrow is a cave. The Rope-Song has a breath where an eighth verse should be. The one open door inside goes down.
hook: Ghorr, the Bone Clan: the hold that kept their name, and the door that goes down to whoever is holding it.

name: Skarl Shieling
unique_feature: a summer shieling of turf huts on the high fell, where Skarl's herders sing the cattle down at dusk
story: The herders live up here from thaw to first snow and sing the cattle down each dusk with the Skarl verse. The cattle know the tune better than the words.
encounter: Tamsk ko-Skarl on the singing stone at dusk
hook: The cattle came down at dusk to a verse nobody sang.

name: Oskel Shieling
unique_feature: a herders' shieling at the head of Oskeld Dale whose peat-fire is kept in all year for the mine's sake
story: Oskel keep a fire burning at the dale head the year round so the mine can see it. They say it is for the herders; the herders say it is for the mine.
hook: The shieling fire went out, and for a night the mine's singing stopped.

name: Skarl Spout
unique_feature: a waterfall that pours out of a hole halfway up a limestone scar, with no stream above it
story: The Skarl Water runs under the moor and comes out of the cliff's face. The Skarl verse says the giants drank here; the Sayers say karst.
encounter: Ossa ko-Skarl at the lip; scree-hags on the scar
hook: Something came out of Skarl Spout with the water: a clan token of no clan.

name: Ruddale Bridge
unique_feature: a limestone arch over Rudd Beck with a Rudd herd-mark cut on every stone
story: Rudd built it so their herds could come down to the Mere's grazing without paying Kharrow's toll at the gorge. Kharrow has never said a word about it, which is how Kharrow says a great deal.
hook: Kharrow's toll-keeper has started standing on Ruddale Bridge, saying nothing.

name: The Red Moor
unique_feature: leaning stones on the moor where Ghast and Kharrow fought in the year of the broken bridge, one stone for each of the dead
story: The one battle in the Rope-Song, and it is sung as a debt, not a victory. Heather grows red on the moor there and nowhere else in the heights.
encounter: Haska ko-Ghast at her bench by the twelfth stone
hook: A new stone stands on the Red Moor, and nobody has died.

name: The Skerry Watch
unique_feature: a drystone look-out on the sea cliff above the Skerries, where Oskel wives watched for the Salt Isles boats
story: The Salt Isles traders came round the north cape to Oskelcrag once, for lead. The look-out is kept swept, though nobody has watched from it in forty years.
encounter: Grenna ko-Oskel in the look-out, facing the sea
hook: Somebody has been sweeping the Skerry Watch, and leaving the broom.

name: The Wading Giant
unique_feature: a giant's ribs and hips standing out of the sea-cliff where the waves have eaten the land away
story: The Oskel clan say the giant walked into the sea to drown the Breath in him, and got as far as his hips.
hook: Each winter's storms uncover more of him, and this winter they uncovered a hand, closed on something.

name: The Frost Moot
unique_feature: a ring of stone seats in a hollow under the Wall where the seven clans met before the Rib Cathedral, with one seat more than seven
story: The Old Moot. The clans stopped meeting here when they could no longer agree how many seats to sweep.
hook: The snow is brushed off one seat every morning, and it is never the same seat twice.

name: The Oskel Rake
unique_feature: a lead-miners' trench cut a mile along the dale-side, with a winding-stone at its head
story: Oskelcrag's lead came out of the rake before the singing shaft was found. The miners left the rake when it began to answer their picks.
encounter: stone-thralls work the rake at night
hook: Picks are heard in the rake at night, and every morning another yard of the vein is open.

name: The Breathing Stones
unique_feature: a ring of standing stones round a shakehole on the moor that draws the air in and lets it out like a sleeper
story: The clans come here to hear the Breath. Children are held over the hole to be breathed on for luck, and the ones who are not afraid are told they will be herders.
hook: The hole has stopped breathing out.

name: The Rope Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on Brindle Edge hung with children's ropes, taller than a man
story: Brindle children are roped to the fell until they can walk the Edge alone. The outgrown rope goes on the cairn, and the cairn has outgrown the oldest herder on the Edge.
hook: A rope has been added that no Brindle family owns, knotted in a fashion nobody has tied for two hundred years.

name: Kharrow Foot
unique_feature: a walled market-field at the foot of the fells where the clans trade with the lowlands, with a bell-post in the middle
story: Skerrow does not let Tollmere's carts up the gorge on market days; the lowlands come to Kharrow Foot instead, and pay blood-price for any quarrel inside the wall.
encounter: none; clan traders with jobs going
hook: The bell-post rang on a day with no market, and every clan came down to answer it.

name: The Bone Ford
unique_feature: a giant's backbone laid across Rib Beck, walked as stepping-stones
story: The Rib Cathedral's giant lost his spine coming down the dale, the clans say, and the beck has been crossing it ever since.
encounter: Orsk ko-Rudd counting the stones from the bank
hook: The vertebrae have been counted at thirty-one for a thousand years; this spring there are thirty-two.

name: The Tappers' Camp
unique_feature: a resin-tappers' camp in the Rib Pines, a clay pot hung on every trunk
story: The clans tap the pines for the pitch that keeps their chain-links from rusting.
encounter: resin-tappers: Aggi ko-Rudd at her pitch-pot
hook: The resin in one stand of pines has come out red, and the tappers will not go near it.

name: The Rust Scar
unique_feature: a limestone scar in Ruddale's side where the water comes out of the rock the colour of rust
story: Ruddow washes its dead's hands in it before burial. The Rudd clan say the fell is bleeding for its giants.
hook: The water ran clear for one day this spring, and every Rudd child born that day has been named for it.

name: The Deadground
unique_feature: grey spoil heaps and roofless ore-sheds below Oskeld Mine, where nothing has grown in a hundred years
story: The mine's waste was tipped here until the goats that grazed it started walking into the shaft.
hook: Grass has begun to grow on the Deadground, in a single line, toward the mine.

name: Ghastfoot
unique_feature: the Ghast clan's arch at the mouth of their dale, with a skull set in the keystone
story: Travellers going up Ghast Dale ask leave of the skull. The ones who do not ask are the ones who come back down in a hurry.
hook: The skull has been taken from the keystone and a clay one left in its place, very well painted.

name: The Drove Chain
unique_feature: two stones on the Low Road with an iron chain slung between them, which the drovers lift for the herds
story: The Ghast and Brindle clans agreed the chain in 1001: a herd passing pays a beast, and a traveller pays a piece of news.
hook: The chain was found lifted and the price paid in news: a name, spoken to the chain-ward by someone he cannot now describe.

name: The Tinkers' Camp
unique_feature: a clanless tinkers' winter camp under the end of Oskel Edge, pots and chains hung ringing from a frame of bones
story: The tinkers mend the clans' pots and chains and belong to nobody. The clans let them winter here because a tinker is the only news that walks.
encounter: tinkers: Pell Kettleby at his mending frame
hook: The tinkers are packing to leave early, and say only that the chains have been ringing with no wind.

name: The Skerr Stone
unique_feature: a broken waystone at the fells' foot, cut in Skerrish on one face and Valish on the other, the Valish chiselled away
story: The first stone of the clans' country on the Low Road. The Brindle clan cut the Valish off in the Charter quarrel of 942 and never put it back.
hook: The Valish has been cut back in overnight, badly, in a hand like a child copying letters.

name: The Clan Stones
unique_feature: seven painted stones on the fellside, one for each clan, and an eighth socket standing empty
story: Where the Moot swore its first peace. Each clan's stone is painted at midsummer by its eldest; nobody paints round the empty socket, and it is always painted.
hook: A stone has been found standing in the eighth socket, unpainted, and no clan will touch it.

name: The Briar's End
unique_feature: the gap where the Thornmarch's briar gives out against the fell, walled across with bones
story: The one place the Thornmarch is not briar. The Woodfolk walled it and the Skarl clan keeps the wall, and neither will say what from.
hook: The bone wall has been pushed outward in the night, from this side.

name: The Watcher
unique_feature: a giant's skull half out of the scree under the Wall, as big as a barn, looking east
story: The Skarl clan say he died watching the Thornmarch, waiting for something to come through it.
encounter: a scree-hag nests in the skull
hook: The skull has turned in the scree, a hand's breadth south, toward the rest of Wickmere.

name: The Black Keep
unique_feature: a clan tower at Skarldale's narrows, burned by two clans at once and left black
story: The Skarl and the Rudd fought over the dale's summer grass for sixty years. The Moot ended it by giving the grass to neither; the keep was burned by both on the same night, and each still says the other lit it first.
hook: Somebody has been relaying the keep's stair stone by stone, at night, and the Moot wants to know which clan.

name: The Winter Cairns
unique_feature: a fellside of small cairns over the herds lost in the Long Winter of 988, one cairn for every beast
story: The Skarl clan count their wealth in these as well as in their living herds: a beast remembered is a beast still owned.
hook: Every morning this month a pebble has been added to every cairn, and there are four thousand cairns.

name: The Dale Watch
unique_feature: a Ghast clan watch-house halfway up the dale, a horn hung at its door
story: Ghast keeps a watch on its own dale because of the bridge: whoever comes up is asked which side of the Moot they stand on.
hook: The horn was blown at midnight, and nobody in the watch-house blew it.

name: The Drovers' Bothy
unique_feature: a drovers' bothy of skerr and turf at the bend of Skarldale, with a fire kept in for whoever comes down with the herds
story: The Skarl herds come down the dale in autumn and spend a night here. The bothy is kept by whichever family came down last.
encounter: Ottar ko-Skarl at the bothy fire; drovers in autumn
hook: The bothy fire was found lit with a herd's worth of hoofprints round it, going up the dale in spring, when nothing goes up.

name: The Moot Beacon
unique_feature: the Moot's beacon on the last tor of Rib Edge, lit to tell the lowlands the clans are sitting
story: When the Moot sits at the Rib Cathedral the beacon is lit, and every hold between here and the Mere keeps its quarrels until the Moot rises.
encounter: Varn ko-Skarl at the beacon's foot, watching the north
hook: The beacon was lit last night, and the Moot is not sitting.

name: The Hanging Falls
unique_feature: a waterfall hanging frozen on the Wall's face at the head of Brakh Gill
story: The clans say it thaws one day a year, the day the giants were breathed in, and runs for an hour.
hook: It thawed this spring on the wrong day, and has been running for a week.

name: Rudd Mill
unique_feature: a mill on Rudd Beck below Ruddow, its wheel housed in a long-house of turf so the beck's roar will not wake the hold
story: Clan Rudd built its mill under a turf roof because the Rudds sleep by day in the winter dark and will not have the wheel heard, and the mill grinds only at night.
hook: The mill has been heard grinding at noon, with the wheel chained and the hold asleep.

name: Kharrow Hole
unique_feature: a limestone cave-mouth in the dale side above Kharrow Foot, its lip hung with the clans' blood-price tallies on strings
story: Where a blood-price is too great to pay in coin the clans hang its tally in Kharrow Hole, and the debt is the cave's to keep until somebody comes to pay it, and the strings go back further than the torchlight.
hook: A tally-string at the mouth has been cut down and the debt on it marked paid, and nobody will say who paid it.

name: The Bier Stone
unique_feature: a flat-topped resting stone on the corpse road from Ruddow to the Rust Scar, a notch cut into its edge for every bier rested on it
story: The Rudd carry their dead from Ruddow to wash their hands in the Rust Scar before they are buried, and the bier is set down here on the way, once, so the dead can look back at the hold. Every rest is notched.
hook: A notch was cut on the stone last week, fresh and deep, and nobody in Ruddow has died.

name: The Wrist Hole
unique_feature: a narrow cave-mouth in the limestone under the Fallen Hand's wrist, blackened by the fires of herders sheltering from the wind
story: The herders say the Wrist Hole goes up inside the giant's arm, and that on a still day you can hear the fingers creak above you. They shelter in its mouth anyway, because it is the only place on that side of the moor out of the wind.
encounter: crag-wolves shelter in the Wrist Hole at night
hook: The herders' fire in the Wrist Hole drew backwards last night, the smoke going in, and the dogs would not follow it.

name: The Patter Stone
unique_feature: a waystone on the Low Road scored all over with tinkers' marks, a pot, a chain, a closed hand, telling the next tinker which holds pay and which set dogs on you
story: The tinkers belong to no clan and write to nobody but each other. The stone is their notice-board: a pot for a hold that has work, a closed hand for one that owes, a dog's head for one to walk past quickly.
hook: A new mark has been scored on the stone that no tinker at the camp can read, and they are packing up early because of it.

name: The Brakh's Eye
unique_feature: a giant's skull half sunk in the verge of the Low Road, the road bending round its brow, one eye-socket heaped with the herders' offerings
story: The Oskel say the skull is what was left when the Breath took the giant back and could not take the weight. Herders going by put something in the eye for him to look at, so that he does not look at them.
encounter: a stone-thrall climbs out of the verge by the skull after midnight
hook: Something has been sleeping curled in the eye-socket, small as a child, and leaving the offerings untouched.

name: The Oskel Drip
unique_feature: a low cave-mouth in the dale side below Oskelcrag where a spring drips out of the limestone into a worn stone basin
story: Every Oskel child is carried down to the Drip in its first week to drink the first water of its life that has not come through the mine. The clan says it is so the child knows what water tastes like before it learns what the mine does to it.
hook: The spring has started coming out of the rock warm, and humming the same note as the mine's singing shaft.

name: The Singing Seat
unique_feature: a Ghast song-shrine on the dale road, a flat stone for the singer to stand on and the small offerings of the forgiven set round its foot
story: Once a year the Ghast sing the song of forgiveness here, for Kharrow's old shaming at the bridge, whether Kharrow likes it or not. Kharrow does not, which is part of why it is sung.
encounter: a scree-hag shrieks from the dale side at dusk
hook: Somebody from Kharrow came and stood on the singer's stone this year and sang the answer, which nobody in Ghast knew had words.

name: The Two-Clan Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on the shoulder of Oskel Edge built half of Ghast's dark stone and half of Oskel's pale, where the herders of both dales can see each other's folds
story: Ghast and Oskel herders meet at the cairn to swap strays and news. Each adds a stone of their own dale's colour, so the cairn is a record of who came more often, and each side says it is the other.
encounter: crag-wolves den on the edge's shoulder
hook: The cairn has been rebuilt overnight all of one colour, a grey that is neither dale's, and neither clan will say who did it.

name: The Horn Hole
unique_feature: a slit of a cave in the side of Ghast Dale where the Dale Watch keeps its spare horn and its winter oil against a siege
story: The Ghast keep a second horn in the rock below their watch-house, so that if the watch is ever taken the dale can still be called. Nobody has ever needed it, and it is kept oiled every autumn anyway.
encounter: a scree-hag on the rocks over the mouth after dark
hook: The spare horn was found blown on the night the Dale Watch's horn sounded with nobody in the watch-house, the mouthpiece still wet.

name: The Pitch-Pot Shrine
unique_feature: a tappers' shrine in the Rib Pines, a stone with a clay resin-pot hung over it and the drips of forty summers run down its face in amber
story: The tappers give the first drip of every tree to the stone, so that no chain the pitch goes on rusts in a shameful hour. The stone is so thick with it now that it glows at sunset.
encounter: a scree-hag hunts the tappers in the Rib Pines after dark
hook: The resin on the stone has come out red this spring, the red of the stand the tappers will not go near, and it is warm to the hand.

name: The Bone-Carvers' Camp
unique_feature: a carvers' camp by the Rib road where splinters of giant bone picked from the beck are laid to dry on a rack beside the fire
story: The Bone Ford sheds splinters in the spring floods, and the carvers camp here to pick them out of Rib Beck and cut the bone tokens every clan-child wears. Each clan has its mark, and a carver who cuts a mark for a clan not his own cuts his thumb first.
hook: The splinters washing down this spring come out of the beck already cut, into tokens with a mark no clan owns, and they keep coming.

name: The Swearers' Rest
unique_feature: a drystone bench on the road up to the Rib Cathedral where oath-takers sit with their sponsors to learn their words, a cairn beside it for each oath kept
story: An oath said wrong inside a giant's bones is said forever, so whoever goes up to swear before the Moot sits here first with a sponsor and learns every word. When the oath has been kept a year the sponsor comes back and adds a stone.
encounter: clanless outriders waylay oath-takers on the Moot road at dusk
hook: Somebody has cut an oath into the bench's back in careful Skerrish, and it is sworn to no clan.

name: The Beacon Shieling
unique_feature: a beacon-keeper's shieling below the tor, a turf-roofed hut and a drystone fold, with peat stacked by the door for the beacon
story: Whoever keeps the Moot Beacon lives up here through the sitting months with a few sheep and stacks peat for the beacon all summer. The beacon has to catch at the first touch, or the lowlands will not know the clans are sitting.
encounter: crag-wolves come for the keeper's sheep after dark
hook: The peat stack was burned to the ground in the night without the beacon being lit, and the keeper was asleep beside it and woke warm.

name: The Oathbreaker's Stone
unique_feature: a broken waystone on the Moot road, its top lying face-up at its foot where a name was chiselled out of it
story: The name of whoever broke an oath at the Rib Cathedral is cut on the waystone below it, and when the clans decide the breaker is gone from their memory the name is chiselled out and the stone struck through. There have been four in a thousand years.
hook: A name has been cut back into the fallen top overnight, in careful Skerrish, and it is the name of a clan chief now living.

name: The Oath-Takers' Fire
unique_feature: a vigil camp below the Rib Cathedral where oath-takers sit the night before swearing; the fire went out at dawn, the way it must, and the cups are still set round it
story: The one who is to swear keeps vigil here and lets the fire go out at dawn, to show the Moot they come with nothing burning. Crag-wolves come down from the Cathedral's skull on the vigil nights, and nobody is allowed to help.
encounter: crag-wolves down from the Cathedral's skull after dark
hook: The fire was found lit this morning, for the first time in anyone's memory, with nobody due to swear.

name: The Unroofed Hold
unique_feature: the roofless shell of a small hold cut half into the dale side above the Clanless Camp, one gable standing and a bone lintel over its door with the clan name hacked off it
story: A Dreugh family's hold, cast out whole when the father could not pay a blood-price and would not hang its tally in Kharrow Hole. They went to the Clanless. The Dreugh took the roof, as the law says, and left the walls, as the law does not.
encounter: a clanless outrider keeps the shell
hook: Somebody has been living in the shell and paying Dreughow a blood-price in firewood, a bundle a night, left at the hamlet's door.

name: Dreugh's Lookout
unique_feature: a lookout cairn on a spur of Swale Edge where Dreughow keeps an eye on the Clanless Camp below, a flat watcher's stone set on its top
story: Dreughow sends a child up to the cairn every evening to count the fires at the Clanless Camp. More fires than yesterday and the hamlet sleeps with its door barred; fewer, and somebody from Dreughow goes down in the morning to find out who has gone. Dreughow keeps a clan bow in the cairn's lee for the child on watch, in case the counting ever turns into something else.
hook: The watcher's stone on top of the cairn has been turned in the night to face Dreughow, not the camp.

name: The Shaft Pebbles
unique_feature: a cairn of river pebbles round a stone on the Oskel's bank, each pebble for an Oskel miner who went down the shaft and did not come up
story: Where the river leaves Oskeld Dale is as far from the shaft as the clan's memory will carry a miner. Every pebble on the cairn is a name, and on the one night a year the mine does not sing the Oskel come down and say every one.
hook: A pebble has been laid for Brenn ko-Oskel, who is still at work underground and sends up word by every shift that he is well.

name: The Cart-Wards' Post
unique_feature: a clan cart-wards' post on the Low Road, a fire and a lean-to where Brindle's warriors wait to walk the ore-carts past the Clanless Camp, their shields stacked by the fire
story: The Clanless take from Brindlecrag's ore-carts and call it blood-price, so every cart that goes by the overhang goes with Brindle warriors walking beside it. The wards wait here between carts and keep the fire in.
hook: The Clanless have stopped taking from the carts, all at once, and the wards cannot find out why, and would very much like to.

name: Brindle's Luck
unique_feature: a stone by the pine road that every Brindle ore-carter rubs with pitch-oil in passing, till it shines like a chestnut
story: The road from Brindlecrag down past the Three Sisters is the steepest the ore-carts take, and a carter who does not oil the stone on the way down does not trust his brake on the way down either, which comes to the same thing.
encounter: clanless outriders watch the ore road from the pines by day
hook: The stone was scraped dull overnight and a clanless man's loosened chain-link left lying on top of it.

name: The Gorge Porters
unique_feature: a porters' camp in the bottom of Kharrow Gorge where loads are shifted off lowland carts onto clan mules for the climb to the Hold
story: No lowland cart goes up Kharrow Gorge on the clans' say. Loads are carried from here to the Hold on mules, by Kharrow porters, at Kharrow rates, and a load that cannot be split between two mules does not go up at all.
encounter: a scree-hag throws stones down the gorge wall at the porters by day
hook: A load was left at the camp addressed to Kharrow Hold in a Tallyman's hand, too heavy for two mules, and it hums whenever the Hold's bell rings.

name: The Link-Keeper's Fire
unique_feature: the link-keeper's fire at the end of the Chain Bridge, the bridge's loosened links hung ringing on a line between two posts in the wind off the gorge
story: When a clan is shamed, one link of its chain on the bridge is struck off and the bridge leans. The link-keeper hangs every struck link here until the shame is paid and the link goes back, and can tell each clan's link by its ring.
hook: Ghast's link went back onto the bridge last night, and the link-keeper did not put it there.

name: The Brother's Seat
unique_feature: a drystone bench on the Low Road with a cairn beside it, looking up to the middle ledge of the Three Sisters where their Hearthstone stands behind the water
story: The Rudd sisters carried the Hearthstone up so that their exiled brother would be remembered somewhere warm. He was not allowed nearer to it than the road, so he built this seat where he could see it, and sat in it until he died.
hook: A clanless man sits in the seat every dusk and weeps, and will not say for whom, and the Rudd have started leaving him bread.

name: The Burned Ore-House
unique_feature: the roofless stone ore-house on the Low Road where Brindlecrag's carts once overnighted, its door burned out and one gable black to the top
story: The Clanless burned the ore-house the first winter they came to the overhang, and called it the blood-price for a Brindle debt none of them would name. The carts have not stopped here since.
encounter: two clanless outriders on the road by day
hook: New-cut roof beams have been hauled up and set across the walls, and nobody in Brindlecrag or at the overhang will say who is building.

name: The Last Cairn
unique_feature: a snow-capped cairn at the head of the Windgate Cleft, the last thing a traveller passes on the way to the pass
story: Travellers going north over the Windgate take a stone from the cairn and put one back if they return. The cairn is the count of those who came back, and it has been shrinking for as long as the gate-warden's family has kept the Watch.
hook: The cairn has been growing all winter, a stone a night, though nobody has crossed the pass in years.

name: The Ice-Cutters' Camp
unique_feature: an ice-cutters' camp on the snow slope below Frostmother's Cradle, the fire went out long ago, saws and sledges still standing in the drift
story: Kharrow Hold cuts its summer ice from the slope below the Cradle, because the ice there does not melt on the way down. The cutters camp for a week each winter and do not go nearer the Cradle than the camp.
encounter: a scree-hag watches the snow slope by day
hook: The ice they cut last winter has not thawed in the Hold's cellars in a whole summer, and each block has a shape frozen in it that was not there when it was cut.

name: The Knotted Rope
unique_feature: a rope-shrine by the Low Road, a stone with a hole through it and a knotted rope tied through the hole, every knot a name somebody wanted kept
story: The clans say memory is a hand on the rope, and this is the rope. A traveller who is afraid a name will be forgotten ties a knot for it and says the name once, and the Brindle who keep the shrine say it again every morning.
encounter: crag-wolves cross the Low Road at dusk below Kharrow Gate
hook: A knot has been untied from the middle of the rope, and the name that was in it is gone from every Brindle's memory but one child's.

name: The Shift Stone
unique_feature: a waystone halfway up the Oskeld mine road, a notch cut into it for every shift that went up and a cross for every shift that did not come down
story: Every shift going up to Oskeld Mine cuts its notch on the way past, and the overseer checks the notches against the shifts coming down. The crosses are few and old, and every Oskel child can say where each one is.
encounter: a clanless hewer waits on the mine road at dusk for the shift's pay
hook: Last week a shift's notch was cut that the overseer did not send up the mine road, and the mine sang all that night.

name: Gann's Shieling
unique_feature: an Oskel goatherd's shieling on the dale floor below the Deadground, a turf-roofed hut and a drystone fold with every beast in it tied by a rope
story: The Oskel stopped grazing the dale below the mine when the goats began walking into the shaft. Old Gann ko-Oskel was the last to leave. This spring he has come back with a new flock, and ties every beast in the fold on its own rope.
encounter: a stone-thrall walks up from the Deadground to the fold after midnight
hook: Every morning the ropes in the fold are found untied and neatly coiled, and every beast is still there, standing facing the mine.

name: The Debtors' Lean
unique_feature: three leaning stones on the Ruddow road below Kharrow Hole, where those whose tallies hang in the cave stop to lean with their backs to it
story: A debtor whose blood-price is too great to pay has its tally hung in Kharrow Hole, and must not look at the cave while passing it. They stop at the stones, lean with their backs to the Hole, get their breath, and go on facing the road.
hook: A debtor was found asleep against the middle stone, facing the Hole, and his tally in the cave has been cut down and marked paid.

name: The Neither Stone
unique_feature: a boundary waystone in Skarldale's summer grass marking the Moot's line, the Skarl mark and the Rudd mark both chiselled off it so that it belongs to nobody
story: The Skarl and the Rudd fought sixty years over this grass, and the Moot ended it by giving it to neither. The stone was set to mark the grass that is nobody's, and both clans' marks were cut off it the same day, by both clans, in front of the Moot.
hook: Both marks have been cut back onto the stone overnight, side by side, in the same hand.

name: The Skarl Skull
unique_feature: a giant's skull lying in the dale's grass beside the track below the Black Keep, its eye-sockets used as a byre for heifers
story: The Skarl say the skull is their giant's and the Rudd say it is theirs. The Moot gave it, like the grass, to neither, and the heifers of both have sheltered in its eye-sockets in bad weather since, which the Moot says was the point.
encounter: crag-wolves wait in the long grass by the skull after dark
hook: The heifers will not go into the sockets any more, and something has been cropping the grass inside them short.

name: The Smelters' Stone
unique_feature: a smelters' shrine under the pines below the Smeltings, a stone where the first ingot of every smelt is laid and left for a night
story: Iron from the top of the vein, lead from the middle and silver from the bottom, the Brindle say, and the first ingot of each goes to the stone for a night, so the fell knows the clan did not take more than it gave back.
hook: The ingot laid last month was taken in the night, and a lead one left in its place, cast in the shape of a hand.

name: The Namers' Fire
unique_feature: the fire where Kharrow youths wait out the night before crossing Kharrow Force's lip, a ring of stones and one stool for the one who waits
story: A Kharrow youth crosses the lip of the Force on the iron rope on their naming day, and waits here the night before, alone, with whoever of the clan will come and sit outside the firelight and say nothing.
hook: A youth waited here all night last week and crossed the lip at dawn, and no clan will own her.

name: The Newsmonger's Stone
unique_feature: a waystone by the Drove Chain chalked all over with the news paid at the chain, washed off by every rain and chalked again
story: The Drove Chain is lifted for a beast from every herd and a piece of news from every traveller. The chain-ward chalks each piece on the stone so the next traveller can read it for nothing, which the Ghast think is theft and the Brindle think is funny.
encounter: crag-wolves come down Ghast Dale to the chain at night
hook: The news chalked on the stone yesterday is next week's, in the chain-ward's own hand, and he says he did not write it.

name: The Old Toll-House
unique_feature: the roofless first toll-house of the Windgate, abandoned when the snow came down the pass, one gable standing out of the drift
story: The Windgate's toll was taken here before the snow came lower every winter and the warden's family moved down to the Watch of the Gate. A toll-house where nobody comes to pay is only a house, and the snow took the roof. The last toll-keeper's axe, bronze from an Oroth bell, is still hung on the toll-shelf, where the snow has not reached it.
encounter: a clanless raider shelters in the old toll-house
hook: Somebody has paid the toll here, at the old house, in coin struck before the Chain Years.

name: The Slag Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn of glassy black slag from the Smeltings on the shoulder of the Brindlecrag road, each lump the size of a fist
story: Every Brindle smelter throws the first lump of slag from their first smelt onto the cairn, so there is a lump there for every smelter the clan has had. The children can name the oldest by their colour.
encounter: a clanless hewer waits for the ore-carts on the shoulder after dark
hook: A lump of slag has been found on the cairn with a silver ring grown up out of the glass, and when it is struck it hums a note the smiths refuse to name.

name: The Listening Stones
unique_feature: three leaning stones bored through on the Oskeld mine road, where the singing of the shaft comes out of the rock
story: Oskel miners put their ear to the holes in the stones before going down, to hear whether the shaft is singing true. A shaft that sings true is a shaft that holds; a shaft singing flat is one to stay out of.
encounter: a stone-thrall stands among the stones after midnight
hook: The stones have started singing on their own when the shaft is quiet, one verse behind it.

name: The First Verse
unique_feature: a waystone at the Dreughow road's last bend painted with the first verse of the Rope-Song, as Dreughow's doors are painted
story: Dreugh sing first at the Moot, and paint the first verse on their doors so a stranger knows the order of things before he knocks. The stone at the bend tells him before he reaches the doors, so he has the length of the road to learn it.
hook: The verse on the stone has been painted over in grey, the grey of the Hush, a word at a time, a word a night.

name: The Raiders' Perch
unique_feature: a lone cairn on a spur above the Windgate track from which the Clanless watch the road to Kharrow Hold
story: The Clanless cannot come to the Hold, so they watch it. From the spur they can see every cart that crosses the Chain Bridge and every traveller on the Windgate track, and a few of them come down to meet the ones they like the look of.
encounter: two clanless outriders keep the perch
hook: The watchers on the spur have been counting the Hold's people, not its carts, and have cut the count on the cairn's cap-stone.

name: The Wolf Stones
unique_feature: three stones on the moor road where the crag-wolves mark their ground, the grass round them worn to a ring
story: The crag-wolves of the High Moor mark the stones as the edge of their hunting, and the Windgate's travellers know it: past the stones at dusk you walk in company, with a torch, and you do not run.
encounter: crag-wolves gather at the stones at dusk
hook: The wolves have started marking the far side of the stones as well, as if the edge of their ground had moved to meet the road.

name: The Hag's Hut
unique_feature: a tumbled herders' hut under the scree on the Ruddow road, roofless, goat bones hung in its one standing gable
story: The Rudd herders used the hut when the flocks were on the scar. A scree-hag took it the winter the herder died, and hangs the bones of the goats she takes where the herder hung his lantern, which the Rudd say is her idea of a joke.
hook: The hag has hung a Rudd herder's lantern back in the gable, lit, and it burns all night.

name: The Scar Cairn
unique_feature: a herders' cairn on the slope over the Rust Scar, topped with a slab set on end, where the Rudd stop with their dead before the washing
story: The Rudd carry their dead down past this cairn to wash their hands in the Rust Scar, and every bearer adds a stone for the one they carry. The cairn is taller than the Bier Stone's notches are long, because the living add stones too, on the day they choose their own bearers.
hook: A stone has been added with a name painted on it in rust, the name of a Rudd child born this spring.

name: The Hold's Last Look
unique_feature: a corpse-road cairn on the Windgate track above the Bier Stone, where a Kharrow bier is turned so the dead see the Hold one last time
story: The Kharrow dead go up the Windgate track to the old burying ground under the Snow Shelter, and at the cairn the bier is turned round so the dead can look back at the Hold across the gorge. Nobody who has carried one speaks until they are past it.
hook: The bearers have started finding the cairn turned, its top slab facing up the pass instead of down to the Hold.

name: The Small-Debts Post
unique_feature: a tally post on the Ruddow road below Kharrow Hole, hung with knotted cords for the debts too small to trouble the cave
story: A blood-price too great to pay goes into Kharrow Hole. The small ones, a borrowed ram, a word said at a wedding, are hung here on the road where they were incurred, and a knot is untied for every part paid, in front of whoever is passing.
hook: Every cord on the post was found untied one morning, all the small debts of Ruddale paid at once, and nobody in the dale has paid anything.

name: The Counting Fold
unique_feature: a drystone fold by Rudd Beck with a stone lean-to against its wall, where the clan herds are counted before they go down to the shore road
story: Rudd herds bound for the Narrows and the market are penned here for a night and counted by a Rudd and a Merrowhithe man together, so neither can say the other's count was wrong, which they both say anyway.
hook: The count came out one beast over this week, a black ewe with no mark, and the two counters have agreed for the first time that she is nobody's.

name: The Ice-Block Cairn
unique_feature: an ice-cutters' marker cairn in the snow below the Cradle, topped with a block of ice that has not melted in any summer
story: The ice-cutters mark the edge of the slope they may cut from with a cairn, and cap it with the first block of each winter. Past it is the Cradle's ice, which keeps what froze in it.
hook: The block on top has something frozen into it this year, a hand held open, and the cutters will not cut past the cairn.

name: The News-Owed Post
unique_feature: a tally post by the Drove Chain hung with knotted cords, a cord for every traveller who crossed without paying the chain its piece of news
story: The Drove Chain is lifted for a beast from every herd and a piece of news from every traveller, and a traveller who has no news has a cord hung here instead, to be untied when they come back with some.
hook: A cord has been untied with a piece of news tied in its place, written on bark, and the chain-ward will not read it out.

name: The Unsaid Post
unique_feature: a tally post on the slope below Kharrow Gate, a knotted cord hung on it for every traveller who would not say the clans' law back
story: The gate-ward sends a traveller who will not say the law down to the Unsayers' Stones for the night. If they still will not say it at dawn, a cord goes on the post, and it stays until they come back and say it.
hook: A single new cord hangs on the post with no knot in it at all, and the gate-ward says that means somebody said the law back in a language he did not know.

name: The Two-Knot Fold
unique_feature: a drystone fold between the Tinkers' Camp and the Brakh's Eye, shared by Ghast and Oskel, its gate tied with a knot of each clan, sheep grazing in it
story: Ghast and Oskel herders share the fold where their dales meet, and each ties the gate with their own clan's knot, so a gate found open means both have agreed to open it, which happens about once a year.
hook: The gate was found open with both knots untied and retied as one knot that neither clan uses.

name: The Forgiveness Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on the Ghast Dale road with a stone for every year the song of forgiveness has been sung at Kharrow, whether Kharrow liked it or not
story: The Ghast add a stone after each year's singing, and the cairn is the count of how long they have been forgiving Kharrow for the bridge. It is a tall cairn.
hook: This year two stones were added, and the second is Kharrow limestone.

name: The Neither Fold
unique_feature: the Drovers' Bothy's night-fold on the Neither Grass, drystone with a lean-to, ewes of both clans penned in it together
story: The Moot gave the Skarldale grass to nobody, and the drovers pen whoever's herd is passing in the fold at night without asking whose. It is the only fold in the fells where a Skarl ewe and a Rudd ewe lie down together.
hook: The drovers found a Skarl and a Rudd herder asleep in the lean-to back to back, and neither will say who came in first.

name: The Peat-Road Cairn
unique_feature: a marker cairn on the Moot Beacon's slope where the beacon-keepers' peat road leaves the Moot road, topped with a slab set on end
story: The keeper of the Moot Beacon brings peat up from the moss by this way, and marks the turning with a cairn so the road can be found in the dark on a night the beacon must be lit.
hook: A line of peat turves has been laid on the road from the cairn to the beacon, one every pace, and they are warm.

name: The Charter-Debt Post
unique_feature: a tally post by the Skerr Stone hung with a single thick cord of many knots, the debt of the Charter quarrel of 942, still owed
story: When the Brindle cut the Valish off the Skerr Stone in the Charter quarrel, the Moot hung the debt on a post beside it. A knot is untied only when a Tallyman and a Brindle shake hands at the post, and it has happened four times in a hundred years.
hook: A knot was untied last week, and neither the Tallymen nor the Brindle will admit to the handshake.

name: The Clanless Fold
unique_feature: a drystone fold the Clanless took and keep on the Low Road, its gate facing the overhang, a stone lean-to built against its wall
story: The fold belonged to Brindle until the Clanless came to the overhang. They took it the first winter and kept it, and they keep it well, which the Brindle find harder to forgive than the taking.
hook: The Clanless have started penning Brindle strays in the fold and sending word up to Brindlecrag to come and fetch them.

name: The Kept-Oaths Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn below the Swearers' Rest on the Moot road, of sponsors' stones moved down from the bench when the bench's own cairn grew too tall
story: A sponsor adds a stone at the Swearers' Rest when an oath has been kept a year. The cairn there grew so tall it hid the view, and the oldest stones were carried down to this one, so the Moot road now passes two cairns of kept oaths and none of broken ones.
hook: A stone has been taken off the cairn and left beside the Oathbreaker's Stone, broken in two.

name: The Winter-Herd Fold
unique_feature: a drystone fold high on the Skarl Fells above the Winter Cairns, with a stone shelter at its wall and a flock of ewes in it
story: The Skarl count their wealth in their living herds and in the Winter Cairns, a cairn for every beast lost in the Long Winter of 988. This fold is where the living flock is brought in, in sight of the cairns, so the living and the remembered are counted from the same hill.
hook: The flock in the fold has grown by a beast every morning this month, and the Winter Cairns have each lost a pebble.

name: The Rudd Anchorite
unique_feature: a hermit's lean-to of boughs against a boulder above the Ruddale road, a stool and a bundle of drying herbs, and a cup set out for whoever climbs up
story: A Rudd woman who lost her whole clan-line in one winter walked up out of Ruddale and never walked down again. She sets out a cup of whatever she has brewed for anyone who climbs to her, and asks only their clan-name, and writes it down.
hook: The anchorite has started asking for the names of the Clanless, too, and writing them in the same book as the clans.

name: The Rudd Mouth Bench
unique_feature: a lookout bench of split stone above the Rudd Mouth road, set where the dale opens and the whole lower Rudd can be seen down to the bridge
story: The Rudd elders sit on the bench to watch who comes up the dale. It was cut long enough for seven, one for each of the old Rudd lines, and they still sit in their order, with the gaps left where a line has ended.
hook: There have been eight on the bench on still evenings, seen from the road below, and the Rudd have only ever had seven lines.

name: The Falls-Road Finger
unique_feature: a shrine of a single finger-bone of a giant set upright in a cairn by the Three Sisters road, the spray of the falls on it on a west wind
story: The falls-folk say the giant who lies under the Three Sisters reached out one last time before he went still, and this is where his finger came through. They wet it with falls-water for luck before a crossing.
hook: The finger has turned in its cairn to point up the dale, away from the falls, and the falls-folk have stopped wetting it.

name: The Clanless Fire-Ring
unique_feature: a raiders' camp of the Clanless on the Fallen Hand road, a fire-ring and hide shelters in a fold of the fell, a bone horn hung on a pole to call the rest
story: The Clanless hold the upper road to the Fallen Hand when the clans are busy at Kharrow. They take a toll in food from whoever walks it, and blow the horn when they see a carry of goods worth the whole band's coming down.
encounter: two clanless raiders keep the fire on the Fallen Hand road
hook: The horn on the pole has been blown at night with no one at the fire, and the Clanless on the road swear they did not blow it.

name: The Oskel Smithy
unique_feature: the roofless ruin of the old mine smithy on the Oskeld road, its forge cold, the anvil still on its stump and a grave-marker of iron slag by the door
story: Before the deep seam was sealed the Oskel mine had its own smith on the road, who shod the ponies and mended the picks. When the mine closed he stayed, and when he died the miners buried him by his door with a marker he had poured himself.
hook: The anvil has been heard ringing in the smithy at night, one blow at a time, and in the morning there is a new shoe on the stump, too small for any pony.

name: The Dreugh-Road Beacon
unique_feature: an unlit clan beacon on a rise over the Dreughow road, its cordwood stacked and its pitch-barrel full, taken and held by clanless hewers
story: The Dreugh laid the beacon to call the dales when Clanless came down the road. The Clanless came down the road, took the beacon so it could not be lit against them, and have sat on it since.
encounter: two clanless hewers sit on the beacon over the Dreughow road
hook: The hewers on the beacon have started stacking more wood on it every day, as if they mean to light it themselves.

name: The Skarl Brow Bench
unique_feature: a lookout cairn on the brow above the Skarl Bridge road, a slab bench on its lee side, from which the Black Keep and the whole of the Skarl can be seen
story: The Skarlow shepherds built the cairn to sit out of the wind while they watched the flocks on the far side. From it you can see the Black Keep across the water, and they say that is why the cairn has never once been rebuilt the same height twice.
hook: The cairn is a stone taller every morning, and there is no shepherd on the fell who will admit to adding it.

name: The Cathedral Spring
unique_feature: a spring let out of the bank through a bone spout into a stone trough on the Rib Cathedral road, a cup of horn on a chain
story: The spring comes out of the dale side just below the Rib Cathedral, and the Merrowhithe folk say the water has run through the giant's ribs before it reaches the trough. They drink it for strength, and never after dark.
hook: The cup on its chain has been found full of warm water at dawn, and the spring has always run cold.

name: The Oskelcrag Peat Bank
unique_feature: a peat bank cut square into the fell above the Oskelcrag road, the turves drying in rows on the heather and a spade left standing in the cut
story: Oskelcrag burns peat because the fell has no wood, and every family has its bank. This one has been cut by the same family for nine generations, the spade handed on with it.
hook: The spade has been left in the cut and nobody has come back for it, and the family's door in Oskelcrag has been shut since the last new moon.

name: Old Ghastow
unique_feature: a Ghast hold of five drum towers on the rise above the Red Moor, roofless since the year of the broken bridge, its gate hung with broken clan chains, one for every exile inside
story: Ghast built it to watch Kharrow's side of the moor and left it the spring after the Red Moor, when there was nobody left in it to keep the watch. The clanless took it forty years ago. Every man and woman the Moot unropes and cannot find walks to Ghastow in the end and hangs the chain their clan broke over them on its gate. The Unroped keep one law of the clans and no other: a price paid is a price paid, whoever pays it and whatever for.
encounter: the Unroped on the walls and round the yard fire; their chief, Gorrm, in the undercroft under the keep
hook: The Moot counts the chains on Ghastow's gate every spring. This spring there is one more chain than there are clanless.

site.hook_prompt: Count the chains on the gate

name: Orrdun
unique_feature: a door cut in the Wall's face above the snowline, framed in a giant's ribs, where the Skarl carried their dead up to lie nearest the Breath
story: The Breath takes the oldest and the deepest first, the clans say, so the Skarl carried their dead as high and as deep as they could, to be first in line. For three hundred years a Skarl memory-keeper went up behind every bier and sang the name in. The last keeper who went up did not come down, and the Skarl stopped carrying. On still nights the herders at the shieling hear her singing yet, and the cattle come down to it.
encounter: the dead the Breath did not take, up and walking in the bone-hall, and the Keener at the bottom still singing names
hook: The herders at Skarl Shieling hear a verse at dusk from the Wall and the cattle come down to it: a Skarl verse, with names in it nobody living has sung.

site.hook_prompt: Read the bier-stone by the door

name: The Brakh's Drink
unique_feature: a low mouth in a limestone scar breathing cold wet air, where the Skarl Water goes under the fell, a giant's knee-bones set either side of it like door-posts
story: The Skarl verse says the giants knelt here to drink before the Breath took them, and that one of them was still drinking when it came. The Skarl Water goes into the fell here and comes out at Skarl Spout, and between the two it runs through a lake nobody has seen the far side of. For a month something has been sending tokens of no clan down the water to the Spout, one a week.
encounter: stone-thralls and scree-hags along the underground water, and at the lake the Kneeling Brakh, still drinking
hook: Something came out of Skarl Spout with the water, and the Spout's keeper knows where the water goes in.

name: Pennant's Weather-House
unique_feature: a Sayer's turf-roofed weather-house on the shore of Blackwater Tarn, vanes and a rain-gauge on posts round it and a bell rigged to ring when the wind turns
story: The Sayers' Circle sent Maudry Pennant up from Tollmere to prove that the clans' Breath is karst: air moving through limestone as it moves through any sponge. She has been on the moor six winters. She has not proved it, and she stopped writing to Tollmere to say so two winters ago.
encounter: Maudry Pennant among her instruments; crag-wolves come down to the tarn to drink at night
hook: The Breathing Stones have stopped breathing out, and the only person on the moor who can measure it does not believe in the Breath.

name: Skerrfall Quarry
unique_feature: a Brindle stone-quarry cut in steps into the fell above Brindlecrag, its last face half-cut round a long white stone that is not stone
story: Brindle cut the lintels for half the holds in the heights here, skerr by skerr. Last autumn the face opened on a giant's shin-bone laid in the rock like a lintel over a door, and the bone was warm to the hand. The quarrymen downed tools. Hodd ko-Brindle, who has run the quarry thirty years, has not, and sits by the face every day waiting for it to tell him whether to go on.
encounter: a stone-thrall that walked out of the new face; Hodd ko-Brindle at his bench
hook: The new face at Skerrfall breathes out on cold mornings, and the Breathing Stones have stopped.

name: The Leadhouse
unique_feature: the roofless lead-house the Salt Isles traders kept above the Oskel shore, its walls grey with old lead-dust and a Salt Isles tide-mark painted over the door
story: When the Salt boats still came round the north cape the Oskel smelted lead for them, and it waited here for the tide. The last boat broke on the skerries the winter the Skerry Watch went dark, forty years ago, and the Salt Isles never came again. The clanless use the house when the wind is in the west, and the heather round it is the only broom-heather on the Oskel shore.
encounter: clanless outriders out of the wind; the Salt boat's last letter under the hearthstone
hook: The heather in the broom left at the Skerry Watch grows at the Leadhouse and nowhere else on the shore.

name: The Frozen Drove
unique_feature: a whole Skarl drove standing in the snow on the Wall, heads up and every one facing north, frozen where it stood fifty-five winters ago, with the drover's crook still upright among them
story: In the Long Winter of 988 a Skarl drove went up the dale in a storm and did not come down, and the Skarl built a cairn on the fell for every beast. This spring the Hanging Falls thawed on the wrong day, the snow on the Wall slumped, and here they are: all of them, standing, facing the Windgate, as if something had called them up the mountain and they had gone to see what.
encounter: crag-wolves that circle the drove all night and will not touch it
hook: A herd's worth of hoofprints went up past the Drovers' Bothy in spring, when nothing goes up, and the wrong thaw has opened the snow on the Wall.

name: The Sorting Ground
unique_feature: a flat of limestone pavement on the moor where giants' bones lie laid out in rows, largest to smallest, by no hand anybody has seen
story: Nothing lay here in the spring. By midsummer the pavement was covered: ribs by length, knuckles by size, a line of vertebrae running from the Giant's Spine's end to the pavement's edge and stopping one bone short. The Bone Ford has counted thirty-two since the spring, and the stone-thralls on the moor have been seen carrying.
encounter: stone-thralls at their sorting, who do not care to have the bones moved
hook: The Bonefield's bones have started to lie in order, and there is a place on the moor where the order is kept.

name: Uldra's Steading
unique_feature: a Skarl hill steading of drystone and turf under the Skarl Ridge, a byre, a peat-stack and a bone lintel over the house door with every child of the house cut in it, and one Valish name among them
story: Uldra ko-Skarl's family have farmed the ridge-foot since the Long Winter emptied the dale and the Moot gave the grazing to whoever would stay. Uldra stayed. She keeps forty sheep, a dog that is mostly wolf, and the only Skarl lintel with a Valish name cut in it, her husband's, who came up from the Mere to buy wool and did not go back down.
encounter: Uldra and her son about the byre; crag-wolves at the fold after dark
hook: Uldra's dog went up the ridge in the night and came back with a drove-bell from a drove that was lost before she was born.

name: The Wall-Keepers' Ring
unique_feature: a low drystone ring on the fell below the Briar's End with two fires in it, one Skarl and one Woodfolk, and a line of white stones laid across the middle
story: The bone wall at the Briar's End is kept by the Skarl and the Woodfolk together, under an agreement older than the Moot that neither side will explain. Each sends one keeper. The two live in the same ring on either side of the white stones, and in eleven years they have not said a word to each other that was not about the wall.
encounter: the two keepers at their two fires; crag-wolves along the wall at night
hook: The bone wall was pushed outward in the night from this side, and each keeper says the other was asleep.

name: The Reckoner's Hut
unique_feature: a Kharrow reckoner's hut on the Edge above the North Road, hung inside and out with the tally-sticks of blood-prices paid and owing
story: When a clan owes a death the Moot asks a Kharrow reckoner what the life was worth: in beasts, in coin, in news, in years of work. Graddo ko-Kharrow has reckoned for thirty-one years and never had a price refused, which he says is the whole of the craft. He lives up here alone, because a reckoner who lives among people starts to reckon them.
hook: There is coin in the Blood-Price Stones' grooves for a death nobody has reported, and the reckoner who set every price on the North Road for thirty years did not set this one.

name: The Broom-Wife's Bield
unique_feature: a single turf bield in the heather under the Wall, a stack of heather brooms at its door and nothing else for a mile
story: Bressa was Oskel once. She kept the Skerry Watch the winter the Salt boat broke on the skerries; the Moot found the watch-fire had not been lit, and unroped her. She has lived up here forty years, and she sweeps the places the clans have stopped using, the Old Moot's seats and the watch she failed, because somebody should, and because nobody can stop a clanless woman sweeping.
encounter: Bressa at her door, binding brooms
hook: Somebody has been sweeping the Skerry Watch, and leaving the broom.

name: The Faceless Graves
unique_feature: a row of long graves on the fell below Ghorrow, their headstones turned face-down into the turf, so whatever was cut on them is cut into the ground
story: The clans do not bury in rows; each clan's dead go to its own ground. These belong to nobody. The Skarl herders say the stones lay face-down when their grandmothers' grandmothers found them, and that whoever turns one over owes the Moot a verse. Nobody ever has.
encounter: stone-thralls that stand up out of the graves after dark
hook: A headstone has been turned face-up in the night, and the mark cut on it is the one on the tokens coming out of Skarl Spout.

name: The Whelping Hole
unique_feature: a shakehole on the moor by the Windgate road fallen in to a cave, its rim trodden bare and white with shed fur, where the crag-wolves bear their young
story: Every spring the crag-wolves come down off the Wall to whelp in the hole, and every spring the gate-warden's people leave them be, because a wolf with young in the hole does not hunt the road. This spring the wolves came early, and the Snow Shelter's bell rang on a clear night.
encounter: a crag-wolf pack with young in the hole, and what they dragged down into it
hook: The shelter bell rang on a clear night; the gate-warden found tracks going to the Whelping Hole, and one set of boots among them.

name: The Going-Up Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn on the Wall's crest above the snow, looking north over the Ice Reach, built of one stone from every clan's ground
story: The clan that went up and never came down built it on their way, the Rope-Song says, a stone from each hold they passed. Whoever is fool enough to climb this high counts the stones. There are nine, and eight clans' grounds to have taken them from.
hook: Somebody has added a stone to the Going-Up Cairn this year, and the lichen on it grows nowhere south of the Windgate.

name: Old Kharrow's Rest
unique_feature: a flat stone on Kharrow Edge worn into a seat, where Old Kharrow set the mountain's name down to get his breath on the way up the cliff
story: Old Kharrow carried the mountain's name up the cliff so the mountain would know it, and set it down here once, halfway, to breathe. The clans say a name set down anywhere leaves a dent. Kharrow children sit in the dent on their naming day and are told not to get comfortable.
hook: Somebody has cut a name in the dent, very small, and it is not the mountain's.

name: The Skarl Drove-Well
unique_feature: a drovers' well on the Skarldale track, a stone trough the length of a byre, and a Skarl drove-bell hung over it for the young beasts to learn
story: The Skarl water their droves here on the way down in autumn and ring the bell while they drink, so the young beasts learn the note that means water. A drove that knows the bell will come to it from a mile off, in any weather.
hook: The bell over the trough rang in the night with no drove on the track, and in the morning the trough had been drunk low.

name: The Unroping Post
unique_feature: the only gibbet in the clans' country, a post and arm by the Oskelcrag road hung not with men but with children's ropes, cut short
story: The clans do not hang people; they have blood-price for that. When the Moot makes somebody clanless their childhood rope is taken down off their clan's cairn, cut at the length they were when they first walked the Edge alone, and hung here for the weather to have. It is the hardest thing the clans do, and they do it by the road so that everybody sees.
hook: A rope has been taken down off the post and knotted back together, in a hitch nobody has tied for two hundred years.

name: Dunnow
unique_feature: the Remembered Hold: three storeys of dressed limestone front stepping back up the foot of the Wall above the Windgate road, rows of windows lit again, a great door under a giant's thigh-bone, the beacon basket burning on its top terrace, and either side of the door the Long Tally, every blood-price the Moot ever set cut in notches of five, with pale rasped patches where names have lately been ground out
story: In the Chain Years the seven clans cut Dunnow into the Wall together to hold the Long Tally, so that no debt would be forgotten and no clan could say it had paid what it had not; the tally-cutters lived in it, and caravans coming down from the Windgate saw its windows lit and knew the clans remembered. When the Moot went to sticks and reckoners the hold was left to its keepers, and forty winters ago the last of them walked down to Kharrow. This autumn the windows are lit again. The clanless who call themselves the Unwritten have taken the hold, and under Kadda the Rasp they are grinding their own names out of the Long Tally, one notch at a time, believing a debt nobody can read is a debt nobody owes.
encounter: the Unwritten at their fire in the yard and on the landing at the door; inside, their camp in the keepers' halls and Kadda at the Long Tally's head; Fenna ko-Dreugh, the last keeper, in her lean-to on the road side
hook: The windows of Dunnow are lit for the first time in forty winters, and the stone-dust under the Long Tally is fresh.

name: Ghaleld
unique_feature: the chain-mine on the bench above Brindlecrag: its headframe two pairs of a giant's ribs stood foot to foot and lashed at the crown, the winding wheel hung between them twelve metres up, the cage at the shaft's stone collar, the capstan ring worn in the turf, rust-red spoil tipped toward the village, and the last length of chain never carried down lying in the grass in a long S
story: Every chain bridge in the heights was drawn from Ghaleld iron, and the Brindle stood a giant's ribs up for the headframe because no timber in the country was long enough. The iron got richer the deeper they went, and redder, and in the year 1001 the last shift broke into the seam the clans now say was never ore at all: the giant's own marrow, gone to iron in the rock. What was lying in it got up. The miners chained it where it stood, with the last length off their own forge, and kept digging round it for a winter, until the Moot shut the shaft. Brakka ko-Brindle still lights the forge at the shaft head every morning, because the Chain Bridge's links are wearing thin and no other iron will hold.
encounter: crag-wolves round the spoil after dark; below, wolves denning in the upper level, scree-hags in the ladderways, stone-thralls at the break, and the Chained Brakh in the marrow
hook: On the board at the collar the last shift's names are still chalked, under the Moot's order nailed over them, and somebody has drawn a line through the order.

name: Oskel Gloup
unique_feature: a sea cave's fallen-in roof a bowshot back from the Oskel cliffs: a black shaft in the moor with the sea booming at its foot and its spray blowing up out of it, a drystone ring round its lip, the Oskel's derrick of two ship's timbers leaning out over it with the rope still reeved, the winchman's house shut, and an iron lamp-bracket on the seaward lip black with new soot
story: The Oskel lowered lead from the Leadhouse straight down the gloup into the Salt Isles boats lying in the cave below, out of the weather, and the winchman lived over the hole. The winter the Skerry Watch was blamed, the Salt boat broke on the skerries with the watch-fire lit, and nobody asked why a master who could see the fire steered for the rocks. Haldo ko-Oskel, the winchman, went down the gloup that spring and never came up to the moor again. On dark nights there is a lamp in the cave's sea-mouth, below the cliff, where no lamp should be.
encounter: clanless on the rim after dark; below, the Lamp's men in the Salt Isles' old cave and their store of the wreck's lead, and Haldo the Lampman at the sea-mouth with his lamp
hook: There is new soot on the lamp-bracket at the gloup's lip, and the rope on the derrick has been spliced this year.
